title: Your Service IP is a lie. Here's how Kubernetes routes it
caption: kube-proxy explained in 40 seconds. Are you running iptables or IPVS mode in your cluster?

scenes.vo: Kubernetes Service IPs are completely fake. No real network card owns that address, so how does traffic ever reach your Pods?
scenes.heading: KUBE-PROXY

scenes.vo: Meet kube-proxy. Think of it as a train switchboard operator living on every single worker node.
scenes.heading: THE OPERATOR

scenes.vo: It watches for new Services, then writes iptables or IPVS rules to send packets directly to healthy Pods.
scenes.heading: HOW IT ROUTES

scenes.vo: Instead of checking manual routing tables, inspect the kube-proxy DaemonSet in kube-system with kubectl.
scenes.heading: CHECK DAEMONSET

scenes.vo: So kube-proxy: runs on every node, programs Linux routing rules, and makes Service IPs actually work. Follow for more plain English Kubernetes!
scenes.heading: KUBE-PROXY
